EX-99.1 2 ex_1029869.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 ex_1029869.htm Exhibit 99.1 Vicore ’ s Phase 2b ASPIRE Trial of Buloxibutid in IPF Passes Pre-Planned Futility Analysis and Remains on Track for Mid-2027 Topline Results Independent Data Monitoring Committee recommends ASPIRE continue without modification; no safety concerns identified Fully enrolled 378-patient trial advances toward 52-week readout Stockholm, Sweden & Cambridge, Mass., October 22, 2026 – Vicore Pharma Holding AB (Nasdaq Stockholm: VICO, Nasdaq US: VCRE), a biopharmaceutical company unlocking the potential of angiotensin II type 2 receptor agonists, today announced that the independent Data Monitoring Committee (iDMC) for the Phase 2b ASPIRE trial of buloxibutid in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) recommended that the trial continue without modification following a pre-planned futility analysis.
ASPIRE continues as planned and remains on track to report 52-week topline results in mid-2027.

With 378 patients enrolled and a 52-week FVC primary endpoint, ASPIRE was built to generate a high-quality dataset, and our focus remains on disciplined execution through database lock and expected topline results in mid-2027,” said Ahmed Mousa, Chief Executive Officer of Vicore Pharma.

“Our cash runway into the second half of 2028 takes us beyond the readout and allows us to plan the next steps for the program and the company.” “The futility analysis was designed to protect patients and allow us to preserve the integrity of the trial, and we thank the iDMC for its independent review,” said Bernt van den Blink, MD, PhD, Chief Medical Officer of Vicore Pharma.
Recruitment was completed ahead of schedule, positioning the company to report topline results in mid-2027.
